question: Name two optional pavement-marking features explicitly labeled in Figure 3D-1 at the roundabout.
model_answer: Direct Answer: Figure 3D-1 explicitly labels "Optional white diagonal markings" (shown in the splitter-island area on the east approach) as an optional feature. It also labels as "Optional" the yellow edge line placed around the inner (left-hand) edge of the circulatory roadway and the YIELD word pavement marking on the approach. Any two of these satisfy the question. Guidance (recommended): - Where a white edge line is used for the circulatory roadway, "it should be as follows (see Figure 3D-1): A. A solid line adjacent to the splitter island, and B. A wide dotted line across the lane(s) entering the roundabout." (The wide dotted white extension is also called out in the figure, though it is a recommended treatment rather than one of the "optional" labels.) Options (permitted): - "A yellow edge line may be placed around the inner (left-hand) edge of the circulatory roadway (see Figure 3D-1)" — this is the feature labeled "Optional" with a leader pointing to the yellow line around the central island. - "YIELD (word) (see Figure 3D-1) and YIELD AHEAD (symbol or word) pavement markings may be used on approaches to roundabouts" — the figure labels the YIELD word marking as "Optional." - Chevron and diagonal markings "may be used on the approaches to and within the circulatory roadway of multi-lane roundabouts to separate traffic lanes, discourage lane changing, and/or compensate for off-tracking of larger trucks and vehicles" — corresponding to the "Optional white diagonal markings" label in the figure. Visual evidence: [Image 1] and [Image 2] show Figure 3D-1 with explicit labels reading "Optional white diagonal markings" (pointing to the hatched white area on the east approach), "Optional" (pointing to the yellow inner circulatory edge line), and "Optional" (pointing to the YIELD word marking), along with the "Wide dotted white extension of circulatory roadway edge line" callout; [Image 3] shows Figure 3D-8 with similar optional chevron/diagonal marking labels at roundabout ramp terminals; [Image 4] shows Figure 3D-3 Sheet 1 labeling "Optional white diagonal markings"; [Image 5] shows Figure 3D-3 Sheet 2 labeling the "Optional yellow edge line and diagonal yellow markings." Citations: - Figure 3D-1 (p.596) - Section 3D.03 Option §4 (p.605) - Section 3D.05 Option §1 (p.605) - Section 3D.02 Option §5 (p.595) - Section 3D.03 Guidance §2 (p.595) - Section 3D.01 Support §4 (p.595)
gold_answer: Optional diagonal markings in the splitter island and an optional wide dotted extension of the circulatory roadway edge line.
